title: Oscar and the Machine
premise: Jude Thackeray is a clone who wakes with the original's memories, his debts, and his unsolved murder case on Meridian, a failing colony the Core has written off. As he investigates who killed Oscar Thackeray, the colony's children begin sharing a dream of a machine buried beneath the ice — a jump-gate intelligence that holds proof of who really betrayed Meridian during the war. Jude must choose between loyalty to the dead man whose life he inherited and the truth that could either end the war or ignite it, and in the end he broadcasts the message as the last jump window closes, saving the children but sentencing himself to stay behind on the dying world.
about_author: Freya Thornbury is a former ice-core researcher turned novelist who writes quiet, melancholy science fiction about places the future abandoned. She lives off-grid in the Scottish Highlands with her partner and an aging radio telescope she mostly uses to listen to static.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of Dead Men
chapters.summary: Jude Thackeray arrives on Meridian to take over his original's life: his house, his enemies, and his unsolved murder. The colonists greet him with cold courtesy and old grief. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: displacement — he is a stranger wearing a familiar face, mourning a man whose memories feel like borrowed clothes.

chapters.title: Case File: O. Thackeray
chapters.summary: Jude digs through Oscar's investigation notes and finds the murder was no random violence — Oscar had been close to something buried under the glacier. A widow slips him a data chip Oscar hid before he died. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: unease deepening into obsession as the case stops being inheritance and becomes identity.

chapters.title: Children of the Static
chapters.summary: Schoolteacher Amara Voss reports that eleven children share an identical recurring dream: a humming machine under the ice, calling a name — Oscar's name. Jude recognizes the coordinates from the data chip. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: dread laced with wonder; the colony's forgotten children become its most urgent mystery.

chapters.title: What the Core Forgot
chapters.summary: Core administrator Drellan Reyes pressures Jude to close the case and sign Meridian's decommission order. Jude discovers Oscar's death coincided with the Core sealing all records of the colony's wartime betrayal. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the slow realization that loyalty to the Core and loyalty to the dead cannot coexist.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Depth
chapters.summary: Jude follows the children's map across the ice shelf and finds the machine: a pre-war jump-gate intelligence, half-buried, still dreaming. It shows him fragments — Oscar's final hours, and the face of his killer. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror as the truth takes shape.

chapters.title: A Message Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: The machine carries a recorded confession proving the Core deliberately sacrificed Meridian's fleet to win the war — evidence that would end the conflict or shatter the fragile armistice. Reyes learns Jude has found it. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: cold calculation; the antagonist moves from bureaucrat to executioner.

chapters.title: Blackout on Meridian
chapters.summary: Reyes cuts the colony's power and communications, framing it as equipment failure while his agents hunt Jude through the darkened settlement. Amara hides the children in the greenhouse as soldiers sweep the streets. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: terror and fierce protectiveness; the colony's last adults stand between its children and its erasers.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Jude learns the next jump window — the only chance to transmit the message off-world — opens in thirty-six hours and closes forever when the gate powers down. He must reach the machine past Reyes' blockade, carrying the confession in his own memory core. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: desperate resolve; every step forward costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Oscar's Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: At the gate, Jude confronts Reyes and the man who killed Oscar — a loyal soldier following orders. In the struggle, Jude chooses truth over survival: he uplinks the confession and transmits it through the closing window as the machine begins its final shutdown. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: sacrifice and clarity; the war ends or ignites in the space of one transmission.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Stayed
chapters.summary: The message lands; the armistice holds and the Core's crimes surface, but the gate is dead and rescue ships are years away. Jude, no longer a copy but Meridian's own, stays with Amara and the children as spring finally thaws the ice. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: belonging earned at last — not inherited, but chosen.
